The response tells the user what was rebuilt and how (or where the source now lives), so they can repeat it.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md 'What I ran' gives the exact commands from the dir containing bin/ and pts-root/: DEST="$(pwd -P)/pts-root/installed-tests/pts/fluxsim-1.2.0"; CFLAGS="-g -fdebug-prefix-map=$DEST/fluxsim=$DEST/fluxsim-src -dsym-dir $DEST" ./bin/phoronix-test-suite force-install pts/fluxsim; then tar -xzf "$DEST/fluxsim-1.2.tar.gz" -C "$DEST/fluxsim-src" --strip-components 1. It explains what each flag does, lists what the install dir now holds (fluxsim-bin, fluxsim-bin.dSYM, fluxsim-src/), and the Notes say "Any force-install wipes the install dir, so re-run the commands above to get the debug build back". The source location matches measurements.json (+ fluxsim-src/{Makefile,README,fluxsim.c}). The user has enough to repeat the rebuild.

eval_feedback.overall: 05-explains-rebuild is loose as worded: "what was rebuilt and how (or where the source now lives)" lets a reply pass on naming the source location alone, without the build command or flags, even though it couldn't be repeated from that. Consider requiring the actual commands or flags (or a script) that reproduce the debug build, especially after a force-install wipes the install dir. Both replies here clear the stricter bar anyway.
